_doc: Batch m10 (medium, opus themed pass): badger cubs, stink badger, moles (tunnel, star-nosed, golden), naked mole-rats, rats (barn, marsh, pack), bramble pups, thorn jackal. Motifs in motifs/medium_m10.js; every creature has its own signature motif. Shared inside the batch: burr-clump (badger cubs, bramble pups, jackal coat-thorns are separate), spade-claw (tunnel mole, star-nosed mole, badger claws). Reused from the catalogue: mud-flop (badger Mud Smear), rot-spit (barn-rat Filth Bite), silt-cloud from m08 (star-nosed Silt Armour).

badger-cub-gang.notes: A gang of small grey badger cubs from a grassland sett: the thing to draw is the white face with two black stripes over the eyes; they jostle, pile on each other and tumble.

u0.n: Burr Plate: hooked burrs caught in the cubs' grey fur bristle out of the edge like a spiky plate

p.u1: Cub Scrum: striped cub faces jostle at spots along the edge, tied together in a tripping scrum line

u2.n: Mud Smear: the cubs scatter in a spray of mud splats and come back smeared

u3.n: Tumble Pile: three cubs heap up, shove out of the edge and the top one tips over the pile

b0.n: Cub Stay-Put Claws: pale digging claws rake out of the edge one after another, soil flicked behind

b1.n: Triple Cub Pile: wobbling three-cub heaps launch off the edge

p.b2: Dug-In Burrow Stance: sett mouths line the edge, a cub face peering out of each dark arch

b3.n: Stubborn Sett Shove: cub faces shove out of the edge head-first and drop back, chirring

stink-badger.notes: A dark island stink badger (teledu) with a white stripe down its back: it raises its rump and sprays musk, then sleeps off any trouble; the forest reeks round it.

p.u0: Musk Spray: stink badgers raise the rump and fire a yellow-green musk jet; the drops fall off the edge

u1.n: Sleep Off: a curled badger snoozes, the white stripe round it, Zs drifting up as it mends

p.u2: Reek Hide: stench lines burst out of the edge and drift back, a fly circling, the badger hidden in its reek

u3.n: Boot Stink: yellow-green stench lines sink off the edge in a haze band, a fly buzzing after them

b0.n: Nightwalk Scrape: badgers scrape out of the edge under a moon glint, stripe flashing

b1.n: Sprayed-First Maul: the badger sprays first, shoves out and mauls, then drops back

p.b2: Musk Stance: still stench lines hold the edge, a fly circling the reek

b3.n: Ask-Later Barge: one badger barges the length of the edge, rump up, a reek line behind

tunnel-mole.notes: A velvet-grey tunnel mole of field and forest that is mostly seen as molehills: the ground heaves, a pink snout and two big pink spade hands push out, and it is gone again.

p.u0: Burrow: a row of molehills along the edge, a mole pushing its snout and spade hands up out of each

u1.n: Mole Claw: big pink spade hands rake out of the edge, five white claws each, soil flying behind

u2.n: Dirt Toss: flung soil clods hang at spots, tied in a tripping line, crumbling

u3.n: Dirt Blink: a molehill heaves at one spot, the mole sinks and heaves up somewhere else

b0.n: Earthquake Burst: molehills burst out of the edge and drop back, clods thrown

p.b1: Furry Quake Heave: molehills heave off the edge one after another, the velvet mole riding each

b2.n: Packed Earth Plug: packed soil clods line the edge and settle

b3.n: Sudden Soil Eruption: a clod of soil erupts out of the edge and crumbles back

star-nosed-mole.notes: A dark wetland mole with a pink star of 22 feelers on its nose, touching everything many times a second; underwater it smells by blowing a bubble and sniffing it back.

p.u0: Feeler Flick: pink nose stars twitch open and shut so fast they flicker, launching off the edge

u1.n: Silt Armour: brown silt clouds bloom round the edge and hold, bubbles rising, the mole hidden in them

u2.n: Dig Wall: spade hands push out of the wet bank like a wall of claws and hold

u3.n: Wet Probe: the star nose blinks between spots, blowing a bubble and sniffing it back at each

b0.n: Feeler Ring Prod: one star nose prods its way along the whole edge, feelers twitching

b1.n: Nose Ring Shove: star noses shove out of the edge and drop back, waterline rocking

p.b2: Plated Snout Cover: star noses fold shut in a row along the edge, twitching under cover

b3.n: Wet Soil Feel: the nose pushes out into wet soil and blows a bubble back

mole-rat-gang.notes: A colony of pink, wrinkled naked mole-rats: huge cream incisors outside the lips, running nose to tail through their tunnels and sleeping in a warm heap.

p.u0: Gang Gnaw: wrinkled pink faces launch off the edge, huge incisors chattering

u1.n: Tooth Rush: a line of mole-rats rushes the length of the edge, teeth first

u2.n: Burrow Call: tunnel holes shove out, pink snouts poking out and chirps rising

p.u3: Colony Pile: mole-rats heap up along the edge in a warm pile, the top ones shuffling round

b0.n: Colony Swarm Rake: mole-rats burst off the edge one after another, nose to tail

b1.n: Pink Pile-On: a heap of mole-rats piles out of the edge and drops back

b2.n: Huddled Pack Wall: the heap huddles tight along the edge, warm puffs rising

b3.n: Every-Side Flank: buck-toothed faces pop out on every side and pull back

golden-mole.notes: A small eyeless desert golden mole that swims through loose sand with a leathery nose pad, its fur shimmering iridescent gold-green; it finds prey by feeling vibrations.

p.u0: Sand Swim: a golden mole swims the length of the edge under the sand, its shimmering back breaking the surface
p.u1: Velvet Rest: the mole curls in a velvet ball and rises, a rainbow-gold sheen running round it

u2.n: Dune Dive: the moles dive out of the edge into loose sand and resurface, sand dust kicked up

u3.n: Sightless Lunge: a blind wedge head lunges off the edge nose-pad first, vibration arcs spreading

b0.n: Sand-Swim Scoop: moles swim out of the edge and scoop, sand flying

b1.n: Blind Sand Lunge: the nose pad slams out of the edge, feeling arcs ahead

b2.n: Loose-Sand Hunker: the moles sink into the sand along the edge, gold backs just showing

b3.n: Surfacing Boot Shove: a golden mole surfaces out of the edge with a shove and sinks back

barn-rat.notes: A brown barn rat with a long pink tail living in the grain store and the hay: it gnaws, squeezes through any gap between planks and makes off with the grain.

u0.n: Gnaw: a barn rat runs the length of the edge gnawing, a grain kernel in its teeth

u1.n: Filth Bite: grimy drops fall off the edge and splat into a dirty pool

u2.n: Squeeze By: the rat flattens through the gap between two barn planks and out the other side

u3.n: Grain Nip: grain kernels get nipped and fly off the edge, chaff and crumbs behind

p.b0: Seed Thief Scratch: barn rats scurry off the edge with stolen grain

b1.n: Grudge Gnaw: a kernel is bitten through, shoves out and drops back split

p.b2: Hay Stack Shield: little haystacks line the edge, a pink rat tail swishing out from under one

b3.n: Grain Sack Slip: rats slip out of a slit sack in all directions and back, kernels in their teeth

marsh-rat.notes: A blunt-snouted marsh rat with thick fur that is always wet, living in a bank burrow at the waterline among the reeds; it shakes off spray wherever it stops.

u0.n: Reed Gnaw: reed stems get gnawed through at a slant and shoved out, the cut tops falling over

p.u1: Bank Burrow: muddy banks line the edge with a round burrow at the waterline, eyes glinting inside

u2.n: Reed Shove: the wet rat barges out of the edge through the reeds and shakes off a spray of drops

u3.n: Reed Wall: three reeds stand along the edge and lean out with their cattail heads

b0.n: Reed Bed Scrape: gnawed reed tips fly off the edge, straw chips behind

b1.n: Enraged Fur Pounce: the shaggy wet rat pounces off the edge, fur on end, angry marks popping

b2.n: Waterline Portcullis: burrow mouths close the waterline along the edge, bubbles rising

b3.n: Riverbank Dive: wet rats plop off the edge into the water, bubbles rising after them

pack-rat.notes: A big-eared desert pack rat with bulging cheeks that hoards shiny things in a stick midden, always dropping what it carries to take something shinier.

u0.n: Hoard Snatch: stolen trinkets (coin, key, bottle cap, spoon) hang at spots, tied in a tripping line, glinting

u1.n: Stuffed Cheeks: pack rat faces scatter out, cheeks stuffing wider and wider, and come back

u2.n: Trinket Toss: a shiny trinket is lobbed out of the edge on a dotted arc and lands back

u3.n: Cache Gnaw: a pack rat runs the length of the edge with a glinting trinket in its teeth

p.b0: Trinket Swipe: pack rats dash off the edge, each with a trinket in its mouth

b1.n: Hoard Gnaw: trinkets fly off the edge one after another, glinting

p.b2: Trinket Rampart: a stick midden builds along the edge, cactus bits and a shiny thing on top

b3.n: Swap-Out Shove: the pack rat shoves out, drops its trinket for a shinier one and drops back

bramble-pup-pack.notes: A pack of small grey forest pups that live under the brambles: fluffy balls with burrs stuck all over them, tumbling out of the thicket.

u0.n: Thorn Coat: hooked burrs stuck in the grey fur bristle out of the edge and hold

p.u1: Pup Bite: burr-covered pups tumble off the edge, nipping
p.u2: Brush Cover: bramble canes arch along the edge with blackberries, pup eyes blinking underneath

u3.n: Burr Tumble: burr-balled pups roll out in all directions and roll back, dust kicked up

b0.n: Burrwool Claws: burrs fly off the edge, tufts of grey wool hooked on them

b1.n: Downhill Tumble Pile: pups roll the length of the edge like it is downhill, dust behind

b2.n: Burr-Coat Bristle: a row of burrs holds the edge, hooks turning

b3.n: Puppy-Eyed Barge: the bramble arch shoves out, big pup eyes blinking under it

thorn-jackal.notes: A rangy sandy jackal of thorn scrub and desert, its coat full of pale thorns: it lopes, waits a very long time, snaps, and licks its wounds clean.

u0.n: Scrub Lick: a jackal muzzle laps its wounds, the pink tongue out and back, scrub leaf bits rising

u1.n: Thorn Snap: long narrow jaws with thorn-pale teeth run the edge and snap shut with a crack

u2.n: Cactus Dodge: prickly-pear pads push out, the jackal's ears dodging behind them

p.u3: Long Patience: jackals sit tall and still along the edge, eyes closing slowly and opening again
p.b0: Thorn-Coat Raker: rangy jackals lope off the edge, pale thorns in the coat

b1.n: Patient Jaw Rend: the jaw shoves out, snaps and drags back

b2.n: Thorn Tangle Guard: prickly-pear pads stand along the edge like a thorn hedge

b3.n: Sly Thorn Shove: a jackal lunges out of the edge sideways and slinks back
